messages.subject: Help with calculateDiffMeth function (2)
parts:
Hi, Altuna

I have used a small script to track back what is going on: 

xdata =methtiles.1.3

  l = dim(xdata)[1]
  percent = c()
  diff = rep(0,l[1])
  pvals = rep(1,l[1])
  for (i in 1:l[1])
  {
    m = matrix(as.numeric(xdata[i,c("coverage1","numCs1","coverage2","numCs2")]),nrow=2)
    percentm = 100*m[2,]/m[1,]
    percent = rbind(percent,percentm)
    diff = percentm[2]-percentm[1]
    pvals = fast.fisher(m)[[1]] # http://code.google.com/p/methylkit/source/browse/#git%2FR
  }

The cycle stop at:

> i
[1] 192

where

> m
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]  809  513
[2,]   NA   51

That is, for some unknown reason, some of the previous functions applied to get the variable "methtiles.1.3" (tileMethylCounts, unite or reorganize) introduced a "NA":

tiles <- tileMethylCounts(methy, win.size = 1000, step.size = 1000)
methtiles <- unite(tiles, destrand = F)
methtiles.1.3 = reorganize(methtiles,sample.ids=c("Sample_1", "Sample_3"),
                      treatment=c(1,0))

It is possible that before application of the function tileMethylCounts, some CpG position could have the values NA. In this case, if tileMethylCounts is not dealing well with the missing values, then the overall count for the given region could be NA. But I could not find the source code for this functions. So, I do not where the missing value could be generated.

All the best,

Robersy

-----------------------------------------------

I am trying to compute the differentially methylated regions with the function calculateDiffMeth. After reorganized the data:

methtiles.1.3 = reorganize(methtiles,sample.ids=c("Sample_1", "Sample_3"),
                      treatment=c(1,0))

I have applied:

mDifMeth.1.3 <- calculateDiffMeth(methtiles.1.3, num.cores = 8)

In my laptop, via RStudio, I got the following message:

"Error in pi0 * length(order_rawp) * order_rawp :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator
In addition: Warning message:
In parallel::mclapply(my.f.list, f.fisher, mc.cores = num.cores) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code"

In my workstation, via command line, direct in R:

"Error in unlist(parallel::mclapply(my.f.list, f.fisher, mc.cores = num.cores)) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'unlist': Error in mcfork() :

(My workstation has 32 GB of memory RAM)

Could you please give me a suggestion on how to solve this issue?

Best Regards,

Robersy

messages.subject: Re: Help with calculateDiffMeth function (2)
parts:
Hi Robersy,
It is hard to guess where the problem might be, but in the tiled data set, there are multiple regions that have coverage but NA values for numCs or numTs. 

Here are some examples:
                         id  chr    start      end strand coverage1 numCs1
193  Chr1.10078001.10079000 Chr1 10078001 10079000      *       637     NA
277  Chr1.10153001.10154000 Chr1 10153001 10154000      *      1478     NA
324  Chr1.10196001.10197000 Chr1 10196001 10197000      *      1229     NA
836  Chr1.10660001.10661000 Chr1 10660001 10661000      *      2285     NA
875  Chr1.10696001.10697000 Chr1 10696001 10697000      *      1438     NA
1098 Chr1.10899001.10900000 Chr1 10899001 10900000      *       125     NA




I guess you need to check CpGs on those regions and see if anything is wrong with the methylRaw objects. You can create a GRanges object with the problematic regions and subset your methylRaw object based on the overlap. If there is nothing wrong with them, you need to check the result of regionCounts() for those regions and if that is correct as well it might be reorganize() function that introduces the NA values, but I don't see how because that just subsets the data.

The unite() function may introduce NAs if you use "min.per.group" option but in that case coverage values should be NA as well. 


Best,
Altuna

An alternative could be to remove the rows with NAs from the "methylBase" object. Is this possible?

Best,

Robersy

Hi Robersy,
You can remove CpGs that contain NA values from methylRaw/methylBase objects by using the "[]" operator

newobj=obj[!is.na(obj$numCs1), ] # subsets the methylBase object by checking if NA values present on "numCs1" column



but you should make sure you understand what those NA values mean, I haven't used BSMAP enough to deduce their meaning. I guess you also see them in the original BSMAP methylation ratio file? not only in the methylKit objects? 


Best,
Altuna

but you should make sure you understand what those NA values mean, I haven't used BSMAP enough to deduce their meaning. I guess you also see them in the original BSMAP methylation ratio file? not only in the methylKit objects? 


Best,
Altuna

Hi, Altuna

These data were previously processed with BSMAP and then the methylation values were extracted with methratio.py. I wonder if the methylKit function read.bismark is able to read a sam file produced by BSMAP.

An alternative could be to remove the rows with NAs from the "methylBase" object. Is this possible?

Best,

Robersy

Here are some examples:

1098 Chr1.10899001.10900000 Chr1 10899001 10900000      *       125     NA




I guess you need to check CpGs on those regions and see if anything is wrong with the methylRaw objects. You can create a GRanges object with the problematic regions and subset your methylRaw object based on the overlap. If there is nothing wrong with them, you need to check the result of regionCounts() for those regions and if that is correct as well it might be reorganize() function that introduces the NA values, but I don't see how because that just subsets the data.

The unite() function may introduce NAs if you use "min.per.group" option but in that case coverage values should be NA as well. 


Best,
Altuna
